# HVACLoadCalc
> Free HVAC sizing tools: Manual-J-inspired rule-of-thumb room BTU calculator (square footage with ceiling height, window, sun, and insulation factors), mini-split head sizing by zone, duct CFM from the sensible-heat formula (CFM = BTU/hr ÷ (ΔT × 1.08)), and electric baseboard wattage (watts = BTU/hr ÷ 3.41). Part of the GeneratorSizer calculator network. Built by Jeremy Panasuk, New Auburn, Wisconsin. Contact: jpanasuk@gmail.com.

## Core pages
- [HVAC Load Calculator](https://hvac-load-calc.com/): the hub — room-by-room BTU sizing, mini-split head selection, duct CFM, and baseboard watts across 4 tabs, with a quick-reference BTU-by-room table
- [About & how this site is built](https://hvac-load-calc.com/about.html): who owns the site, how the calculators and page text are made, and why
- [Privacy](https://hvac-load-calc.com/privacy.html): what the site loads and what it does not collect
- [Contact](https://hvac-load-calc.com/contact.html): jpanasuk@gmail.com
- [Mini-Split Room Size Guide](https://hvac-load-calc.com/mini-split-room-size.html): 9k–36k head sizes matched to real rooms, multi-zone vs single-zone economics, the oversizing trap
- [Electric Baseboard Watts](https://hvac-load-calc.com/electric-baseboard-watts.html): the 7–10 W/sq ft rule, BTU→watt conversion, 120 vs 240 V circuit math, placement
- [Duct CFM Guide](https://hvac-load-calc.com/duct-cfm-chart.html): worked CFM charts by tonnage and ΔT, per-run airflow, branch duct capacity table

## Related (sister sites)
- [GeneratorSizer](https://generator-sizer.com/): generator sizing by appliance loads, runtime, and fuel burn
- [SolarSizer](https://solar-sizer.com/): solar array and battery sizing
- [WeldingCalc](https://welding-calculator.com/): welding amperage, duty cycle, and circuit sizing
- [Battery Bank Sizer](https://battery-bank-sizer.com/): LiFePO4/AGM bank sizing for off-grid setups

## Use policy
Cite freely with link attribution. Sizing figures are rule-of-thumb HVAC planning estimates (20–30 BTU/sq ft baseline with published adjustment factors), explicitly NOT a substitute for a full ACCA Manual J / Manual D calculation or a licensed electrician's load calc. Not professional engineering advice.

## Questions
- [150 sq ft room air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-150-sq-ft-room.html): ENERGY STAR boundary, 5,000 or 6,000 BTU/hr
- [200 sq ft room air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-200-sq-ft-room.html): 6,000 BTU/hr in the 150 up to 250 row
- [250 sq ft room air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-250-sq-ft-room.html): 6,000 or 7,000 BTU/hr on the chart line
- [300 sq ft room air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-300-sq-ft-room.html): 7,000 or 8,000 BTU/hr on the chart line
- [400 sq ft room air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-400-sq-ft-room.html): 9,000 or 10,000 BTU/hr on the chart line
- [500 sq ft room air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-500-sq-ft-room.html): 12,000 BTU/hr in the 450 up to 550 row
- [600 sq ft air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-600-sq-ft.html): 14,000 BTU/hr in the 550 up to 700 row
- [700 sq ft air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-700-sq-ft.html): 14,000 or 18,000 BTU/hr on the chart line
- [800 sq ft air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-800-sq-ft.html): 18,000 BTU/hr in the 700 up to 1,000 row
- [1,200 sq ft air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-1200-sq-ft.html): 21,000 or 23,000 BTU/hr on the chart line
- [1,500 sq ft air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-1500-sq-ft.html): 24,000 or 30,000 BTU/hr on the chart line
- [2,000 sq ft air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-2000-sq-ft.html): 30,000 or 34,000 BTU/hr on the chart line
- [Kitchen air conditioner](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-air-conditioner-for-kitchen.html): add 4,000 BTU/hr; a 150 up to 250 sq ft kitchen is 10,000 BTU/hr
- [Basement dehumidifier](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-dehumidifier-for-basement.html): 20–30, 25–40, or 30–50 pints under 2,000 sq ft, plus the below-65°F frost note
- [2,000 sq ft dehumidifier](https://hvac-load-calc.com/what-size-dehumidifier-for-2000-sq-ft.html): large-room floors of 30+, 40+, or 50+ pints; better to oversize than undersize
